text: a license to use the methods, procedures and products developed by us in the business of selling and servicing Unit Franchises
rationale: Licence of company-developed methods is a standard franchisor grant; no one-sided burden.

text: The rights granted herein include the limited right to sublicense the use of the Proprietary Marks to Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "right to sublicense the use of the Proprietary Marks" extends company marks to sub-franchisees.

text: you shall not have the right to sublicense, sublease, subcontract or enter into any management agreement providing for the right to operate the Franchised Business or to use the System
rationale: "shall not have the right to sublicense" protects the company's system and marks.

text: 1.3.2 To own, acquire, establish and/or operate, and license others to establish and operate, businesses under other proprietary marks or other systems, whether such businesses are the same, similar, or different from the Franchised Business
rationale: Reserved company right to operate other proprietary-mark businesses; favourable to the company.

text: 1.3.1 To own, acquire, establish, and/or operate, and license others to establish and operate, other Franchised Businesses at any location outside of the Master Territory.
rationale: Company reserves right to franchise "at any location outside of the Master Territory"; favourable to company.

text: 1.3.3 To license others to sell or distribute any products or services which bear any proprietary marks, including the Proprietary Marks, at any location outside of the Master Territory.
rationale: Company reserves right to license marks "outside of the Master Territory"; favourable to company.

text: 7. NON-COMPETITION
rationale: Rule: restrictions on company business need approval. "NON-COMPETITION" section may bind the company's own activity.

text: 7.1 Restrictions
rationale: Rule: restrictions on company business need approval. "7.1 Restrictions" scope unclear as to whether it limits the company.

text: D - Confidentiality and Non-Competition Agreement
rationale: Rule: restrictions on company business need approval. Attached non-compete exhibit requires review of who is bound.

text: 5.1 Sale of Unit Franchises; Minimum Development Quota
rationale: Minimum quota obligation falls on franchisee and benefits the company; no adverse one-sidedness to company.

text: E - Minimum Development Quota
rationale: Minimum development quota binds the franchisee; supports company's growth with no adverse effect.

text: 4.2 Continuing Fees Payable to Us
rationale: Continuing fees payable to the company are favourable; no unusual deviation identified.

text: 5.17 Developments are Our Property
rationale: "Developments are Our Property" keeps company IP with company; consistent with playbook.

text: 11.4 Payment of Monies Due; Liquidated Damages
rationale: Rule: pre-set damages need legal approval. "Liquidated Damages" amounts must be reviewed for enforceability.

text: 17. APPLICABLE LAW
rationale: Governing law section may select a forum or law differing from company's home jurisdiction; confirm acceptability.

text: 17.1 Choice of Law
rationale: "17.1 Choice of Law" may deviate from company's preferred jurisdiction; requires review against market practice.

text: 12.1 Transfer by Us
rationale: Rule: assignment needs both parties' consent. "Transfer by Us" may allow unilateral transfer without consent.

text: 12.2 Transfer by You
rationale: Franchisee transfer restrictions are standard and protect company's interest in the franchisee.

text: 11.8 Compliance with Post-Term Covenants
rationale: Post-term covenant compliance protects company's system; standard franchise provision.

text: You shall pay us a renewal fee in the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000) for the right to renew this Agreement.
rationale: Flat-rule deviation: "renewal fee in the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars" is a payment for renewal rights, which is unusual for franchisee-side terms.

text: we may offer to renew this Agreement upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement for the extended term
rationale: One-sided rule: "we may offer to renew" gives franchisor discretion, so renewal is not guaranteed to the company.

text: Your right to extend the term of this Agreement shall be subject to your continued compliance with the terms and conditions in this Agreement as well as your compliance with the conditions set forth in Section 3.2 of this Agreement.
rationale: One-sided rule: renewal is "subject to your continued compliance" plus Section 3.2 conditions, adding extra hurdles.

text: If you do not elect to extend the term of this Agreement, this Agreement shall terminate at the end of the term then in effect.
rationale: Standard expiration: "this Agreement shall terminate at the end of the term" if no extension is elected. Market-typical.

text: You shall pay to us a royalty fee based on revenue generated by Unit Franchisees (the "Unit Franchise Performance Royalty Fee") equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate royalty fees paid to you by Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory pursuant to their Unit Franchise Agreements.
rationale: One-sided rule: "twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate royalty fees" paid to franchisor on unit franchisee revenue is a large revenue share.

text: You shall pay to us a franchise sales royalty fee (the "Franchise Sales Royalty Fee") for each Unit Franchise you sell in the Master Territory as follows: twenty-five percent (25%) of the initial franchise fee collected from each Unit Franchisee upon execution of the Unit Franchisee's Franchise Agreement
rationale: One-sided rule: "twenty-five percent (25%) of the initial franchise fee" payable to franchisor on each unit sale.

text: The National Advertising Fund Contribution shall be collected by you from each Unit Franchisee and spent by you in accordance with the agreement on behalf of the franchisor and Franchisees.
rationale: Ambiguous rule: "collected by you from each Unit Franchisee and spent by you" creates fund-management duties with unclear accountability.

text: Fees and Royalties cannot be increased or decreased without our prior written consent.
rationale: One-sided rule: "cannot be increased or decreased without our prior written consent" restricts company pricing flexibility.

text: You shall only use and serve soups that are approved by us and must be purchased from suppliers designated or approved in writing by us
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "must be purchased from suppliers designated or approved in writing by us" needs business and legal approval.

text: Soups shall be cost plus 25% FOB the supplier.
rationale: Pricing rule: "cost plus 25% FOB the supplier" fixes a markup on soup purchases, limiting margin control.

text: In order to keep your exclusivity
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "In order to keep your exclusivity" is an incomplete condition with unstated obligations, requiring approval.

text: $170,000.00 of soup from us in 2015
rationale: One-sided rule: "$170,000.00 of soup from us in 2015" is a fixed purchase minimum on the company.

text: $5,000,000.00 of soup from us in 2018 and shall increase 10% each year thereafter.
rationale: One-sided rule: "$5,000,000.00 of soup from us in 2018 and shall increase 10% each year" is a large, compounding minimum commitment.

text: We maintain the right to open and operate new company units and to sell franchises to our existing franchisees.
rationale: Competitive rule: "right to open and operate new company units" and sell to existing franchisees undermines company's territorial exclusivity.

text: (f) We shall be permitted to sell branded products to national accounts without any money due to you or your parent company. Once you have units open and operating in the trade area where a National Account is located, we will remit to you 25% of the profits derived from the sales in that specific trade area.
rationale: Profit Sharing rule: one-sided obligation. "we will remit to you 25% of the profits" shifts national-account revenue, conditioned on unit openings.

text: We will not grant other franchises nor establish our own Unit Franchises within the Master Territory during the term of this Agreement unless you do not meet the Minimum Development Quota.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: needs business and legal approval. "We will not grant other franchises" binds the company within the Master Territory.

text: If you do not meet the Minimum Development Quota, we may cancel your exclusive right to market and sell Unit Franchises in your Master Territory and may sell additional Master Franchises within your Master Territory, or we may begin operations of our own in your Master Territory, or we may terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: needs business and legal approval. "we may cancel your exclusive right" with broad remedies including company operation.

text: you must sell and have open the minimum number of The Original Soupman businesses as set forth on Attachment E hereto (the "Minimum Development Quota") by the dates set forth on such Attachment.
rationale: Minimum Commitment rule: largely franchisee-facing and customary. "Minimum Development Quota" with fixed dates is standard.

text: You must charge your Unit Franchisees the initial franchise fee, royalty fee, National Advertising Fund Contribution and any other continuing fees that we designate or require, within the limits established by all regulatory agencies which now or hereafter may have jurisdiction over the sale of franchises and the requirements imposed by this Agreement. Any deviations from these amounts must be pre- approved by us.
rationale: Price Restrictions rule: company-favorable and bounded. "Any deviations from these amounts must be pre-approved by us" is customary.

text: 5.5 Insurance   During the term of this Agreement, you shall maintain in force under policies of insurance issued by licensed insurers approved by us insurance coverage as we from time to time require.
rationale: Insurance rule: one-sided and open-ended. "as we from time to time require" allows unilateral changes to coverage.

text: in no event in an amount less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) aggregate.
rationale: Insurance rule: market-standard floor. "not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) aggregate" is reasonable.

text: 5.5.2 As it relates to the operation of your Franchised Business: automobile liability insurance coverage, including owned and non-owned vehicles, with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence;
rationale: Insurance rule: market-standard limit. "not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence" is typical for auto.

text: The insurance policies required herein shall: (a) name us as an additional named insured and contain a waiver of all subrogation rights against us, our affiliates, and our and their successors and assigns; (b) provide for thirty (30) days' prior written notice to us of any material modification, cancellation, or expiration of such policy;
rationale: Insurance rule: standard protections. "name us as an additional named insured" with subrogation waiver and notice is customary.

text: Should you, for any reason, fail to procure or maintain the insurance required by this Agreement, as such requirements may be revised from time to time by us in writing, we shall have the right and authority (without, however, any obligation to do so) immediately to procure such insurance and to charge same to you, which charges shall be payable by you immediately upon notice together with a ten percent (10%) administrative fee.
rationale: Insurance rule: common step-in right. "ten percent (10%) administrative fee" is within normal market practice.

text: You shall expend not less than $5,000 each month on such Solicitation Advertising.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided terms, but "not less than $5,000 each month" burdens the counterparty, not the company.

text: You acknowledge and agree that any such concept, process or improvement shall become our property and we may utilize or disclose such information to other master franchisees and unit franchisees as we determine to be appropriate.
rationale: Company IP rule concerns assignment away from company; "shall become our property" moves rights to the company.

text: We shall own all intellectual property and other rights in the System Website and all information it contains, including the domain name or uniform resource locator ("URL") for the System Website, the log of "hits" by visitors, and any personal or business data that visitors (including you and your personnel) supply.
rationale: "We shall own all intellectual property" in the System Website keeps IP with the company, consistent with the rule.

text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, we reserve the right to inspect or examine your accounts, books, records and tax returns, at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice to you.
rationale: Playbook flags deviations from market practice; "with or without prior notice" and tax return access exceed typical audit terms.

text: You further acknowledge and agree that we may inspect your Franchised Business and any Unit Franchise in the Master Territory to verify that your Franchised Business and/or such Unit Franchise is operating in compliance with our System, as it may be modified from time to time.
rationale: Inspection to "verify... compliance with our System" is standard franchise practice, not a material deviation.

text: during the term of this Agreement, and for a continuous uninterrupted period commencing upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, regardless of the cause for termination, and continuing for a period of three (3) years thereafter, neither you nor your principals shall, directly or indirectly
rationale: Rule covers restrictions on the company's activity; this binds "you nor your principals", not the company.

text: Divert or attempt to divert any business or customer of the Franchised Business or any Unit Franchisee anywhere, by direct or indirect inducement or otherwise
rationale: One-sided: binds franchisee only, "anywhere" with no limit shown; flag under one-sided rule.

text: Employ or seek to employ any person who is at that time employed by us or by any other master franchisee or unit franchisee in the System, or otherwise directly or indirectly induce such person to leave his or her employment without our written consent.
rationale: One-sided employee non-solicit binding only franchisee, "seek to employ" is broad; flag under one-sided rule.

text: Own, maintain, operate, engage in, or have any interest in any business which is the same as or similar to the Franchised Business, or any other business which performs any type of child tutoring services, anywhere.
rationale: Rule covers company's business restrictions; this restricts "you" and "anywhere" but not the company.

text: Each of the foregoing covenants shall be construed as independent of any other covenant or provision of this Agreement.
rationale: Independent-covenant clause restricts franchisee; it does not limit company activity under the rule.

text: Nothing in the Franchise Agreement shall limit our right to maintain websites other than the System Website or to offer and sell products and services under the Marks from the System Website, another website or otherwise over the Internet without payment or obligation of any kind to you.
rationale: Carve-out favors company, letting it sell online "without payment or obligation of any kind to you."

text: prohibitions on your and your employees posting or blogging comments about the Franchised Business or the System, other than on a website established or authorized by us
rationale: One-sided restriction on franchisee and employees benefits company; no company-side obligation identified.

text: We alone will be, and at all times will remain, the sole owner of the copyrights to all material which appears on any System Website we establish and maintain
rationale: Company retains ownership: "We alone will be... the sole owner"; no IP assigned to counterparty.

text: You shall, at our option and request, and without any additional consideration, assign to us all rights to all e-mail addresses, URLs, domain names, Internet listings, and Internet accounts related to the Franchised Business
rationale: Assignment runs to company ("assign to us"), not away from it; favors company.

text: Any and all goodwill arising from your use of the Proprietary Marks shall inure solely and exclusively to the benefit of us or our affiliate
rationale: Goodwill "shall inure solely and exclusively to the benefit of us"; favors company.

text: The right and license of the Proprietary Marks granted under this Agreement to you is non-exclusive
rationale: Non-exclusive license is standard and preserves company's freedom to license others.

text: with the authorized sub-license of the Proprietary Marks to your Unit Franchisees
rationale: Sub-license to "your Unit Franchisees" lets third parties use marks, reducing company control over brand use.

text: We shall have the right, at all reasonable times, to inspect the products and services on which the Proprietary Marks shall be used as we consider necessary to carry out the purposes of inspection as part of appropriate quality control.
rationale: Inspection right "at all reasonable times" favors company as quality control.

text: you shall not directly or indirectly contest the validity of, or our ownership of the Proprietary Marks
rationale: No-contest covenant "shall not directly or indirectly contest" protects company's mark ownership; no legal remedy waived by company.

text: specific identification of us as a third party beneficiary of such covenants with an independent right to enforce them
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided or off-market terms. "independent right to enforce them" favors us, the beneficiary, so exposure is minimal.

text: specific identification of us as a third party beneficiary of such covenants with the independent right to enforce them
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided or off-market terms. "independent right to enforce them" benefits us as beneficiary, so it poses little risk.

text: If any purported assignment or transfer of any direct or indirect interest in this Agreement, in you, or in all or substantially all of the assets of the Franchised Business is made to any third party without our prior written consent, contrary to the terms of Section 12 of this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: assignment needs consent of both parties. "without our prior written consent" requires only our consent, not mutual consent.

text: If an approved transfer, as required by Section 12.6 of this Agreement, is not effected within the time provided following a death or permanent incapacity (mental or physical).
rationale: Rule: change-of-control terminations need approval. "not effected within the time provided following a death" creates a termination trigger requiring approval.

text: If you fail to obtain or maintain required insurance coverage and do not obtain such coverage within ten (10) days after written notice from us.
rationale: Rule: flag off-market or one-sided terms. "within ten (10) days after written notice" gives a reasonable cure period, consistent with market practice.

text: If you fail to comply with the Minimum Development Quota.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "If you fail to comply with the Minimum Development Quota" lacks any cure period or materiality qualifier.

text: We will allow you to use the Proprietary Marks in the Master Territory, subject to the limitations and restrictions set forth in this Agreement, and to use the processes, methods, materials, equipment and promotional plans developed by us.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "processes, methods, materials, equipment and promotional plans developed by us" imposes broad licensing obligations on us.

text: We shall provide the Manuals to you, on loan, for the term of this Agreement and any renewals hereof.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "on loan, for the term of this Agreement" is a standard, limited obligation with no unusual exposure.

text: you shall require and obtain execution of covenants similar to those set forth in this Section 7 (including covenants applicable upon the termination of a person's relationship with you)
rationale: Rule: restrictions on company's business need approval. The clause restricts franchisee personnel, not our business activity.

text: In addition to the foregoing, upon termination of this Agreement by us for cause as described in Section 10, you agree to pay to us within fifteen (15) days after the effective date of this Agreement's termination
rationale: Pre-set payment to company, "agree to pay to us"; favors company, but playbook requires legal approval of liquidated damages.

text: The parties hereto acknowledge and agree that it would be impracticable to determine precisely the damages we would incur from this Agreement's termination
rationale: Impracticability acknowledgment supports company's damages; playbook still requires legal approval of pre-set damages.

text: The liquidated damages provision only covers our damages from the loss of cash flow from the Royalty Fees.
rationale: "only covers our damages from the loss of cash flow" narrows company's recovery under the pre-set damages rule.

text: You shall have no right to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook 90-day convenience notice rule is not triggered; "no right to terminate this Agreement" for franchisee.

text: We shall have the right to assign this Agreement and all of our attendant rights and privileges to any person, firm, corporation or other entity provided that
rationale: Playbook requires mutual consent to assignment; "We shall have the right to assign" is unilateral.

text: may merge, acquire other corporations, or be acquired by another corporation;
rationale: Describes merger rights only; no counterparty termination or renegotiation on change of control is stated.

text: neither you nor any immediate or remote successor to any part of your interest in this Agreement, nor any individual, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity which directly or indirectly owns any interest in you shall not sell, encumber, assign, transfer, convey, pledge, merge, or give away any direct or indirect interest in this Agreement, in you, or in all or substantially all of the assets of the Franchised Business.
rationale: Bars franchisee transfers without consent, matching playbook; "shall not sell, encumber, assign, transfer" protects company.

text: Any change in the control of you shall be deemed a transfer for purposes of this Agreement.
rationale: Franchisee change of control deemed transfer, which favors company; no counterparty termination right stated.

text: You shall not grant a security interest in the Franchised Business or in any of the assets of the Franchised Business without first obtaining our prior written consent.
rationale: Requires company's "prior written consent" for security interests, aligning with the consent rule and protecting company.

text: the executor, administrator, or personal representative of such person shall transfer such interest to a third party approved by us within twelve (12) months after such death or disability.
rationale: Estate transfer requires company approval, "approved by us", within twelve months; consent-based and company-protective.

text: at our option, assume management and control of the Franchised Business during such twelve (12) month period and shall be paid a reasonable monthly management fee for our services as determined by us.
rationale: Change Of Control rule: franchisor may "assume management and control" for twelve months and set the fee itself, a one-sided renegotiation right needing approval.

text: Our consent to a transfer shall not constitute a waiver of any claims we may have against the transferring party
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: clause only preserves claims ("shall not constitute a waiver"); it does not alter the mutual consent requirement.

text: Transfer by You in Bankruptcy - Right of First Refusal
rationale: ROFR rule: bankruptcy-triggered "Right of First Refusal" deviates from market practice and is one-sided against the franchisee.

text: we shall thereupon have the prior right and option, to be exercised by notice given at any time prior to the effective date of such proposed assignment and assumption, to accept an assignment of this Agreement to us
rationale: ROFR rule: "prior right and option... to accept an assignment... to us" is one-sided, though it is a standard franchisor step-in.

text: You and we acknowledge and agree that we are a third-party beneficiary to all Unit Franchise Agreements between you and Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory
rationale: Third Party Beneficiary rule: "third-party beneficiary to all Unit Franchise Agreements" is one-sided, though common in master franchise deals.

text: You shall include in the standard Unit Franchise Agreement used by you a provision which states that we are a third-party beneficiary to the Unit Franchise Agreement and are entitled to the rights granted in this Section 13.
rationale: Third Party Beneficiary rule: requiring "a provision" in every unit agreement adds one-sided drafting burden on the master franchisee.

text: To Franchisor: Kiosk Concepts, Inc.
rationale: Parties rule: "To Franchisor: Kiosk Concepts, Inc." is a routine notice party identification with no one-sided terms.

text: To Master Franchisee: The Grilled Cheese Truck, Inc.
rationale: Parties rule: "To Master Franchisee: The Grilled Cheese Truck, Inc." is a routine notice party identification with no one-sided terms.

text: This Agreement shall be interpreted and construed under the laws of the State of New York.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "laws of the State of New York" is a standard, mutual governing-law selection.

text: In the event of any conflict of law, the laws of New York shall prevail, without regard to the application of such state's conflict of law rules.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "without regard to the application of such state's conflict of law rules" is a common, neutral formulation.

text: The parties agree that any action brought by either party against the other in any court, whether federal or state, shall be brought within the County of New York, State of New York at the time the action is initiated, and the parties hereby waive all questions of personal jurisdiction or venue for the purpose of carrying out this provision.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "waive all questions of personal jurisdiction or venue" departs from typical forum terms and limits defenses for either party.

text: maintain stop transfer instructions on your records against the transfer of any equity securities
rationale: Rule: assignment requires both parties' consent. "stop transfer instructions" concern securities records, not assigning the Agreement, so the rule is not triggered.

text: Attachment A to  Master Franchise Agreement
rationale: Document title is a neutral label; no deviating or one-sided terms appear.

text: KIOSK CONCEPTS, INC.:
rationale: Party name block is standard identification; no one-sided obligations appear.

text: THE GRILLED CHEESE TRUCK, INC.
rationale: Party name block is standard identification; no one-sided obligations appear.

text: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement on the date first shown above.
rationale: Relies on "the date first shown above", which may not exist, leaving the execution date ambiguous.

text: COMMENCEMENT DATE: Upon approval of the State of New York.
rationale: "Upon approval of the State of New York" has no outside date, so the start date is open-ended.

text: each hereby waive to the fullest extent permitted by law, any right to, or claim for, punitive or exemplary damages against the other and agree that, in the event of a dispute between them, each is limited to recovering only the actual damages proven to have been sustained by it.
rationale: Mutual ("each") so symmetric, but limits to "actual damages" with no 12-month fees cap.

text: PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT
rationale: Rule: market practice. "PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT" is a neutral title with no substantive terms.

text: This Agreement, entered into this the 10th day of January 2000, by and between INTEGRITY INCORPORATED, a Delaware corporation with principal offices at 1000 Cody Road, Mobile, Alabama ("Integrity") and TIME LIFE, INC., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Time Life Music, with principal offices located at 2000 Duke Street, Alexandria, Virginia 22314 ("TL").
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Delaware corporation" party identification is standard and raises no deviation.

text: TL guarantees to purchase from Integrity a minimum of ten thousand (10,000) units of each recorded Product during the first thirty-two (32) months of release. TL's initial order for each recorded Product shall be a minimum of five thousand (5,000) units.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "TL guarantees to purchase" a minimum of 10,000 units creates a firm purchase commitment.

text: TL will hold exclusive worldwide rights to promote and sell the product through the following distribution channels: Outgoing telemarketing, General Market retail, and General Market catalogs, and exclusive rights within the United States for Television Direct response.
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "exclusive worldwide rights" to TL across multiple channels requires business and legal sign-off.

text: Integrity will hold exclusive worldwide rights to promote and sell the product to/through the following distribution channels: Christian retail (CBA or Christian Booksellers Association markets), direct mail (including continuity sales, church sales, digital and e-commerce sales.)
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "Integrity will hold exclusive worldwide rights" needs business and legal approval.

text: release shall be simultaneous (i.e., television and direct response will have a period of exclusivity before the products are available at retail).
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "period of exclusivity before the products are available at retail" delays retail availability.

text: The parties agree that the initial suggested retail selling price for the products will be $19.95 for CD's, $17.95 for Cassettes, and $19.95 for song books. Any change in the suggested retail selling price will be mutually agreed by the parties.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Any change in the suggested retail selling price will be mutually agreed" keeps pricing balanced.

text: Integrity may adjust the prices charged to TL on each volume to accurately reflect the then-current royalty obligation to all parties, including Integrity.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Integrity may adjust the prices charged to TL" gives unilateral pricing control.

text: Mechanical rates will not exceed [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of the then-current statutory rate, and Print licenses will not exceed a prorated portion of [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of the retail selling price
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Mechanical rates will not exceed" caps royalties; key figures are redacted, so impact cannot be fully assessed.

text: provided the quantity of such purchases does not exceed seven percent (7%) of the total royalty bearing units of such Product title purchased by TL
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "does not exceed seven percent (7%)" caps TL's purchase volume and limits flexibility.

text: Integrity will pay to TL royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by Integrity in the United States pursuant to this Agreement
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Integrity will pay to TL royalties" sets per-unit economics; redacted amounts prevent full assessment.

text: On sales of printed products (song books) pursuant to this Agreement (less any returns) Integrity will pay to TL royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by Integrity in the United States pursuant to this Agreement
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "royalties in the amount of" for song books, net of returns, with redacted rate needs review.

text: On sales of products pursuant to this Agreement (less any returns) TL will pay to Integrity royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by it pursuant to this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "TL will pay to Integrity royalties" creates a payment obligation; redacted rate limits assessment.

text: Either party, at its sole expense, upon at least thirty (30) days written notice (and not more than once in respect of any accounting period) will have the right to inspect the other party's books regarding the obligations hereunder for a period of two (2) years from the date on which any statement is rendered.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Either party" audit rights, mutual with once-per-period limit, are standard.

text: Integrity shall have the right to license distribution of the Product through all channels of distribution throughout the remainder of the world.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "all channels of distribution throughout the remainder of the world" overlaps TL's exclusive grants.

text: 7.       Sound Recording Copyright and Trademark License.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Sound Recording Copyright and Trademark License" is only a heading; no substantive terms shown.

text: TL and Integrity will jointly develop the repertoire
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "jointly develop the repertoire" creates shared IP ownership ambiguity without stated allocation.

text: This agreement shall commence as of date first above written
rationale: Flag rule: market deviation. "as of date first above written" is vague but common and mutual.

text: shall Continue through December 31, 2004 ("the Term")
rationale: Flag rule: market deviation. "through December 31, 2004" is a fixed, mutual term, which is standard.

text: Thereafter, the parties must mutually agree in writing to extend the term for additional periods of time.
rationale: Flag rule: one-sided obligations. "the parties must mutually agree in writing" makes renewal balanced.

text: Integrity hereby grants to TL the right to use its "Integrity Music" name and logo ("the Integrity Trademarks') in connection with the products produced during the Term of this Agreement for as long as the parties continue to sell and distribute such products at no additional cost to TL
rationale: Flag rule: one-sided obligations. "at no additional cost to TL" with open-ended duration grants uncompensated, indefinite use of marks.

text: TL hereby grants to Integrity the right to use its "TL Music" name and logo ("the TL Trademarks") in connection with the products produced during the Term of this Agreement for as long as the parties continue to sell and distribute such products at no additional cost to Integrity
rationale: Flag rule: one-sided obligations. "at no additional cost to Integrity" with open-ended duration grants uncompensated, indefinite use of marks.

text: the copyright in the Product sound recording compilation will be jointly registered by Integrity in the names of Integrity and TL.
rationale: Flag rule: joint IP ownership deviates from market. "jointly registered" copyright in "names of Integrity and TL" creates shared control.

text: TL will trademark the series name in joint names of TL and Integrity.
rationale: Flag rule: joint IP ownership deviates from market. "in joint names of TL and Integrity" splits trademark control and complicates enforcement.

text: Either party may, at its election, assign this Agreement or any of its rights or delegate any of its obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, to any person, firm or corporation owning or acquiring all or a substantial portion of its assets
rationale: Assignment rule violated. "Either party may, at its election, assign" without consent of both parties.

text: the other party may upon six-months (6-months) written notice terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Assignment rule: consent required. "the other party may upon six-months written notice terminate" allows unilateral exit without consent.

text: This Agreement has been entered into in the State of Tennessee, and the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee
rationale: Flag rule: market deviation. "governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee" is a neutral, common choice.

text: The venue for any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or breach thereof, shall be the appropriate state and federal courts located in Nashville, Tennessee.
rationale: Flag rule: market deviation. "appropriate state and federal courts located in Nashville" is a standard venue choice.

text: INTEGRITY INCORPORATED
rationale: Flag rule: one-sided obligations. "INTEGRITY INCORPORATED" is a party identification with no substantive obligation.

text: TIME LIFE, INC.
rationale: Flag rule: one-sided obligations. "TIME LIFE, INC." is a party identification with no substantive obligation.

text: Oceanic Time Warner Cable and Watchit Media Content and License Agreement
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. Document title "Content and License Agreement" is standard; no deviation found.

text: Watchit agrees to provide Oceanic Time Warner Cable the following content:
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "Watchit agrees to provide" is a standard content-supply obligation.

text: Effective Dates: September 1, 2006, August 31, 2007
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. A one-year term ("September 1, 2006, August 31, 2007") is ordinary.

text: This agreement will be in effect until the end of 2006 and will be evaluated at that time.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "will be evaluated at that time" leaves renewal and evaluation criteria undefined.

text: In the event that Oceanic Time Warner Cable removes the above content and or terminates this agreement prior to December 31, 2006, Oceanic Time Warner Cable agrees to pay a cancellation fee of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000) per month multiplied by the number of months remain on the agreement.
rationale: Rule: no termination for convenience on under 90 days notice. "terminates this agreement prior to December 31" has no notice period.

text: Watchit shall have the exclusive right to sell third party advertising as sponsors of their content
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "exclusive right to sell third party advertising" requires business and legal sign-off.

text: will have the right to brand the content under the Watchit brand and place a "bug" on the screen identifying the content with a Watchit trademark.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "place a 'bug' on the screen" with Watchit trademark is a one-sided branding right.

text: Oceanic Time Warner Cable will use the content solely on channel 777, the Las Vegas channel.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "solely on channel 777" is a narrow, reasonable usage restriction.

text: RESELLER AGREEMENT
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "RESELLER AGREEMENT" is a neutral title with no operative terms.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies, Inc., a Nevada corporation having an address at 5100 W. Copans Road Suite 710 Margate, FL 33063 USA ("MEDIANET GROUP TECHNOLOGIES"), authorizes International Direct Response, Inc., a Pennsylvania Corporation, having an address at 1125 Lancaster Avenue, Berwyn, PA 19312("RESELLER")
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: party identification is standard and creates no one-sided obligations.

text: entered into as of the 19 day of March, 2004
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "entered into as of the 19 day of March, 2004" is a standard date recital.

text: continue for a period of 1 year after the Effective Date
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "continue for a period of 1 year" is a common, neutral initial term.

text: This Agreement shall renew for successive 1-year periods, after the initial 1 Year Term, if agreed by both parties in writing within 30 days of license expiration.
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "if agreed by both parties in writing" makes renewal mutual and consensual.

text: Either party may terminate the Agreement on 60-days written notice during a renewed term.
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "Either party may terminate" on 60 days notice is mutual and market-standard.

text: The laws of the State of Florida shall govern this Agreement, without reference to conflicts of law provisions.
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: "The laws of the State of Florida" is a neutral, commonly accepted governing law.

text: Reseller may nat assign or otherwise transfer this Agreement without MediaNet Group Technologies's prior written consent except to a successor.
rationale: Assignment rule requires both parties' consent; "Reseller may nat assign... except to a successor" is one-sided with a carve-out.

text: Reseller is hereunder licensed to market MediaNet Group Technologies' Brand-A-Port portals ("PORTALS") and to resell MediaNet Group Technologies products and services for compensation
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: "licensed to market... and to resell... for compensation" lacks territory, scope, or exclusivity limits.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies is the exclusive holder of and shall retain, all right, title and interest in and to the Portal, Content and Engine and the All Pages
rationale: IP rule: "exclusive holder of and shall retain, all right, title and interest" keeps company IP and does not assign it.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies shall pay Reseller a fee in accordance with the annexed Fee Schedule.
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided obligations: company must "pay Reseller a fee" per an annex not provided for review.

text: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO EACH OTHER OR ANY OTHER ENTITY FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, HOWEVER CAUSED, ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY
rationale: Liability cap rule requires a cap of at least 12 months' fees; this clause only excludes consequential damages and sets no cap.

text: 13.10 NO DISPARAGEMENT. Each party agrees that, during the Term of this Agreement and for a period of five (5) years thereafter, neither will make written or oral comments regarding the other that are negative, disparaging
rationale: Non-disparagement rule: "for a period of five (5) years thereafter" is a long post-term tail, though mutual.

text: The Reseller Agreement can be terminated at any time at the discretion of either party.
rationale: Termination rule: "at any time at the discretion of either party" sets no 90-day notice minimum.

text: issues a check for 20% commission to the reseller on product sales and 10% the total amount of hosting/maintenance sales made
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: 20% and 10% commission rates appear within ordinary market range.

text: Commissions are only paid each month if the amount owing exceeds $100 US.
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: "only paid each month if the amount owing exceeds $100" withholds sums below a threshold.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies reserves the right to change the level of commission
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: "reserves the right to change the level of commission" is a unilateral, one-sided change right.

text: BRAND-A-PORT OR BSP PORTAL SALES: MediaNet shall remit to Member Provider 20% of the price of each Portal sold directly by it.
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: 20% portal remittance is a standard commission term, not a deviation.

text: BSP MONTHLY HOSTING FEES: In addition, MediaNet shall remit to Member Provider an amount equal to 10% of the hosting fees paid by Buyers
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: 10% hosting-fee remittance is a conventional rate with no one-sided mechanics.

text: MediaNet shall remit all sums due to Member Provider within 30 days of receipt of cleared funds.
rationale: Revenue-sharing rule: payment "within 30 days of receipt of cleared funds" is a standard remittance timeline.

text: MediaNet shall permit Member Provider or its designees reasonable access during normal business hours and, upon request, to verify funds and payments due pursuant to this Agreement.
rationale: Audit rule: only "Member Provider or its designees" may verify, creating one-sided audit access.

text: Resellers are licensed to market the Brand-A-Port applications and receive commission on all product sales
rationale: License rule: "licensed to market" with commission on sales is an ordinary reseller grant.

text: The Reseller will then have 5 months to bring the registered prospect to contract. If a contract is not consummated in the allotted time-frame, the prospect shall then revert back to MNG.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "5 months to bring the registered prospect" implies prospect exclusivity requiring business and legal approval.

text: Retail $495 License Wholesale $395
rationale: Price rule: fixed "Retail $495" and "Wholesale $395" may deviate from market and raise resale-price concerns.

text: executed effective as of the day and year last set forth below
rationale: Effective-date rule: "day and year last set forth below" leaves the effective date ambiguous until signing.

text: MEDIANET GROUP TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
rationale: Parties rule: party name stated plainly; no deviation from market practice identified.

text: Reseller Agreement
rationale: Document-name rule: "Reseller Agreement" is a neutral title with no deviation.

text: Exhibit A to the IP Agreement: List of Assigned Patents
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. Only the title "List of Assigned Patents" is provided, so the assignment scope cannot be verified.

text: ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT
rationale: Rule: market practice. "ENDORSEMENT LICENSING AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT" is a standard document title with no deviation.

text: by and between Marine MP, LLC ("Lender"), for services of Arnold Schwarzenegger ("Endorser"), and Fitness Publications, Inc. ("Fitness")
rationale: Rule: market practice. Standard party identification with no unusual or one-sided terms.

text: is entered into on July 26, 2013 (the "Effective Date")
rationale: Rule: market practice. "entered into on July 26, 2013" is a routine effective date.

text: The Term shall commence on July 23, 2013 and shall expire on July 22, 2016
rationale: Rule: market practice. "shall expire on July 22, 2016" gives a standard three-year initial term.

text: shall automatically be renewed for an additional term of three (3) years (the "First Additional Term")
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "shall automatically be renewed" for three years locks in the company unless it acts to end the term.

text: shall automatically be renewed for an additional term of three (3) years (the "Second Additional Term")
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "shall automatically be renewed" for a second three-year term extends the lock-in further.

text: the Agreement shall expire and terminate automatically without further notice on July 22, 2019
rationale: Rule: market practice. "expire and terminate automatically" on 2019 reflects the first renewal end date, which is routine.

text: the Agreement shall expire and terminate automatically without further notice on July 22, 2022
rationale: Rule: market practice. "expire and terminate automatically" on 2022 reflects the second renewal end date, which is routine.

text: MusclePharm shall not produce during the Term (and any renewal Term, if any) any diet pills and/or sexual enhancement products

text: the AS Parties shall have a right of first refusal (exercisable by written notice to MusclePharm within 15 days after receipt of the Sample) to include such new Product in the AS Product Line
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "right of first refusal" on new Products in the AS Product Line favors the AS Parties.

text: Endorser also agrees to the use on a world-wide basis (as specified pursuant to Section 6 below and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement), during the Term, of his Name and Appearance Rights to advertise and promote the business of MusclePharm, its Products, and the Licensed Products.
rationale: Rule: market practice. Worldwide name rights granted to MusclePharm for its own promotion is a standard license grant.

text: the license to MusclePharm with respect to distribution and promotion of the Licensed Products is on a worldwide basis through the Distribution Channels
rationale: Rule: market practice. "worldwide basis" distribution license benefits the company and raises no concern.

text: MusclePharm shall have the right to use, worldwide, Endorser's Name and Appearance Rights (as specified in Section 6) to advertise MusclePharm and its Products and Licensed Products in print media
rationale: Rule: market practice. Worldwide print-media advertising rights granted to MusclePharm are favorable and standard.

text: MusclePharm also shall have the right to use, worldwide, Endorser's oral or written endorsements of Products and Licensed Products
rationale: Rule: market practice. Worldwide right to use endorsements is a standard grant favoring the company.

text: the right to use Endorser's Name and Appearance Rights granted to MusclePharm in this Section shall extend for six (6) months beyond the expiration of this Agreement
rationale: Rule: market practice. "six (6) months beyond the expiration" is a sell-off period favorable to the company.

text: Endorser shall receive ten percent (10%) of Net Sales (as defined below) from the sale of any Products other than the Licensed Products featured and sold directly in conjunction with the Training Video
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Endorser shall receive ten percent (10%) of Net Sales" on non-licensed products is a sizable revenue share.

text: In the event that MusclePharm shall sell any Promotional Products above its cost then Endorser shall be entitled to receive 10% of Net Sales from the sale of such Promotional Products
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Endorser shall be entitled to receive 10% of Net Sales" on Promotional Products above cost.

text: the marketing budget to promote the Licensed Products shall be $5.0 million during each Contract Year of the First Additional Term
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "marketing budget ... shall be $5.0 million during each Contract Year" is a fixed, recurring spend commitment.

text: the Endorser agrees that he shall make four (4) personal appearances ("Appearances") in the First Contract Year
rationale: Rule: market practice. "four (4) personal appearances" is an obligation on the endorser, a modest and routine commitment.

text: it being understood that there shall initially be no less than four (4) Products at the start of the Term and thereafter no more than 8 (eight) Products in the AS Product Line without the mutual written agreement of the parties hereto
rationale: Rule: restriction needs approval. "no more than 8 (eight) Products in the AS Product Line" caps product scope without mutual agreement.

text: the AS Parties grant to MusclePharm the right to use the Trademarks as defined in this Agreement and the Name and Appearance Rights
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: grant runs to MusclePharm ("grant to MusclePharm the right to use"), so no adverse obligation is apparent.

text: During the Term of this Agreement, the AS Parties grant to MusclePharm and consent to MusclePharm's commercial use of the Name and Appearance Rights to advertise, promote, endorse and publicize Products, Licensed Products, and MusclePharm's business, worldwide in any media selected by MusclePharm
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: broad "worldwide in any media selected by MusclePharm" favors the company's use rights.

text: MusclePharm shall pay Lender a royalty (the "Royalty") of 10% on Net Sales (as defined below) of Licensed Products sold through its wholesale Distribution Channels or retail Distribution Channels
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: 10% royalty on Net Sales is a material ongoing cost; benchmark against market rates.

text: If MusclePharm sells any Licensed Products to any party affiliated with MusclePharm, or in any way directly or indirectly related to or under the common control with MusclePharm, at a price less than the regular price charged to other parties, the Royalty payable to Lender shall be computed on the basis of the regular price charged to other parties.
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: affiliate sales royalty computed on "regular price" regardless of actual price, broadening the payment base.

text: Receipt or acceptance by Lender (or its authorized representative) of a royalty statement or receipt or acceptance of any accompanying royalty payment shall not prevent Lender from at any time within three years after the Term of this Agreement questioning the validity or accuracy of such royalty statement or payment.
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: Lender may challenge statements "at any time within three years after the Term" despite acceptance.

text: Lender shall be entitled to receive a guaranteed minimum royalty for each Contract Year including the Additional Term, if any (the "Guaranteed Minimum Royalty")
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: "guaranteed minimum royalty for each Contract Year" payable regardless of sales, including the Additional Term.

text: Endorser shall also supply MusclePharm with at least fifty (50) signed items for each Contract Year
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: Endorser's duty to supply "at least fifty (50) signed items" benefits the company.

text: Nothing in this Section 6(c) shall entitle MusclePharm to reduce Endorser's compensation pursuant to Section 7 and Section 8 of this Agreement (including, without limitation, with respect to any renewal Term, if any).
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: "shall entitle MusclePharm to reduce Endorser's compensation" is barred, even in any renewal Term.

text: MusclePharm's obligations for the payment of a Royalty and the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty (as defined below) shall survive expiration or termination of this Agreement and will continue for so long as MusclePharm continues to manufacture, sell or otherwise market the Licensed Products.
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided terms: royalty obligations survive "for so long as MusclePharm continues to manufacture, sell", an open-ended tail.

text: Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement for pursuant to Section 9 herein, Endorser shall have no further obligation to render any services whatsoever.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "no further obligation to render any services" is a mutual, ordinary post-termination term.

text: MusclePharm shall not be liable to pay any compensation for services performed after the expiration or termination.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "shall not be liable to pay any compensation" protects the company after termination.

text: shall continue to pay Endorser the Royalty set forth in paragraph 7 herein
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "shall continue to pay Endorser the Royalty" creates an open-ended payment duty after termination.

text: All formulas used in the Licensed Products shall remain the property of MusclePharm, but all rights in any packaging, promotional materials, and websites of the Licensed Products (including, without limitation, pictures, the name, logos and trade dress) and all intellectual property of the AS Parties shall revert back or otherwise be vested in the AS Parties

text: none of the PHL  Parties or any of their Affiliates shall own (1) any information about ICC
rationale: Restricts ownership of information about ICC; no transfer of company IP to counterparty.

text: ICC or one of its Affiliates, as applicable, is the owner of all rights, title and interests
rationale: "ICC or one of its Affiliates... is the owner of all rights" retains ownership; no assignment away from company.

text: the Licenses shall  not extend to sales and distribution of the GIE after the effective date of termination  pursuant to Section 15.02.1
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: license "shall not extend to sales and distribution" after termination restricts post-termination use.

text: (1) the License granted to ICC and its Affiliates shall terminate on the date on which the only remaining Certificates in force are those under which  benefit payments have commenced
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: affiliate license ends when "only remaining Certificates" have benefit payments commenced, a non-standard trigger.

text: (2) the License granted to the PHL Parties and their  Affiliates, restricted as noted in this subsection, shall terminate on the date on which the  last benefit payment is made under the last Certificate in force
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: PHL license runs until "last benefit payment is made under the last Certificate," an open-ended duration.

text: continue only as necessary to make benefit payments under such Certificates
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "only as necessary to make benefit payments" is narrow and tied to existing obligations.

text: the grant of all Licenses shall continue  only as necessary for the Parties to carry out their respective duties and obligations  under the Transaction Documents, as applicable.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: licenses continue "only as necessary" for duties under Transaction Documents, which is balanced.

text: A Licensee shall obtain the  prior written consent of the Licensor for the use or public release by such Licensee of any materials  bearing the Licensor's licensed marks.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "prior written consent of the Licensor" for public use of marks is customary brand protection.

text: A Licensor may revoke a Trademark Consent or the prior written consent provided pursuant to  Section 9.02.5(b) only in the event of a material change in circumstances
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: Licensor may revoke consent "only in the event of a material change," limiting licensor flexibility.

text: such Licensee does not own the Licensor's  licensed marks and claims no rights therein other than as a Licensee under this  Agreement
rationale: Company IP rule: "claims no rights therein other than as a Licensee" confirms licensor ownership, so no assignment occurs.

text: ICC acknowledges that (1) ICC and its Affiliates may benefit from sale of the GIE
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "may benefit from sale of the GIE" is an acknowledgment with no added obligation.

text: the Sales and General Agency Agreement
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "the Sales and General Agency Agreement" is only a document title with no substantive obligation.

text: provided, however, that the Investors Capital Indemnitees and the PHL Indemnitees are expressly intended to be third-party beneficiaries under this Agreement.
rationale: Indemnitee third-party beneficiary status is market standard; "expressly intended to be third-party beneficiaries" is not one-sided.

text: Each of the PHL Parties and their Affiliates, on the one hand, and ICC and its Affiliates, on the other, shall be deemed to be an independent contractor as to the others for all purposes.
rationale: Mutual independent-contractor language, "deemed to be an independent contractor as to the others," is standard and balanced.

text: Except as otherwise expressly set for in this Agreement, no Party shall in any manner be prevented or bound to refrain from engaging in any business or businesses of any kind or nature
rationale: Clause removes restrictions on business activity rather than imposing them; "no Party shall ... be bound to refrain" is favorable.

text: this Agreement shall remain in  effect for so long as any Certificate remains in force with respect to which benefit payments thereunder have not commenced
rationale: Open-ended term, "for so long as any Certificate remains in force," ties duration to third-party certificates; confirm against market practice.

text: This Agreement may be terminated by either the PHL Parties, on the one hand, or ICC, on the other, with respect to Certificates that have not been issued as of the effective date of termination in the following manner:
rationale: Either PHL Parties or ICC may terminate for convenience; the excerpt states no 90-day notice period, so verify compliance.

text: The place of arbitration shall be Hartford, Connecticut.
rationale: Arbitration seat in "Hartford, Connecticut" is a neutral, ordinary venue choice; no one-sided effect is evident.

text: EXHIBIT A TO THE STRATEGIC ALLIANCE AGREEMENT
rationale: Flag-deviation rule: "EXHIBIT A TO THE STRATEGIC ALLIANCE AGREEMENT" is a neutral document title with no obligations.

text: PHOENIX LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY     INVESTORS CAPITAL CORPORATION
rationale: Flag-deviation rule: "PHOENIX LIFE INSURANCE COMPANY" and "INVESTORS CAPITAL CORPORATION" are simply the named parties; nothing one-sided.

text: all as of the Effective Date.
rationale: Flag-deviation rule: "as of the Effective Date" is a standard effective-date reference with no unusual terms.

text: By any of the PHL Parties, on the one hand, or ICC, on the other, providing one hundred and twenty  (120) days prior written notice to the other Parties.
rationale: Termination-notice rule: "one hundred and twenty (120) days" exceeds the 90-day minimum, so it complies.

text: Any of the PHL Parties assigns or transfers this Agreement in a manner that does not comply with the provisions of this Agreement.
rationale: Assignment-consent rule: no explicit consent requirement; "does not comply with the provisions" leaves the consent standard unclear.

text: ICC assigns or transfers this Agreement in a manner that does not comply with the  provisions of this Agreement.
rationale: Assignment-consent rule: "ICC assigns or transfers" lacks express mutual written consent language; relies on unclear compliance reference.

text: No Party shall assign this Agreement or any  rights or obligations hereunder or, except as expressly set forth in the Agreement with respect to the PHL Services  and Investors Capital Services, delegate any of their respective duties and obligations hereunder, without the prior  written consent of the other Parties, which, in view of the unique and specialized nature of each Party's obligations  hereunder, may be declined by any Investors Capital Party on the one hand or any PHL Party, on the other hand, as  the case may be, for any reason.
rationale: Assignment-consent rule: mutual consent required, but "may be declined... for any reason" and delegation carve-out create broad veto.

text: A Change of Control, as defined below, shall be considered an assignment under this Section 16.01 and Sections  16.02.1(c) (4) and 16.02.1(e)(4).
rationale: Change-of-control rule: CoC treated as assignment under "Sections 16.02.1(c)(4) and 16.02.1(e)(4)", enabling termination rights.

text: A "Change of Control" means:
rationale: Change-of-control rule: definition header "A 'Change of Control' means:" sets up triggers that may enable counterparty termination.

text: the acquisition by any person, entity or group, including a "group" required to file a Schedule 13D or  Schedule 14D-1 under the 1934 Act
rationale: Change-of-control rule: "the acquisition by any person, entity or group" has no ownership threshold, so it is very broad.

text: the election or appointment to the board of directors of any member of the Control Group, or resignation of  or removal from such board of directors with the result that the individuals who as of the date hereof  constituted the board of directors
rationale: Change-of-control rule: board "election or appointment" or "resignation of or removal" triggers are broad and tied to termination.

text: the approval by the shareholders of any member of the Control Group of:
rationale: Change-of-control rule: "the approval by the shareholders of any member of the Control Group" is a broad trigger with no threshold.

text: 16.04 Governing Law. text: 1. LIMITED LICENSE: Nothing in the Agreement or this Exhibit shall be construed to grant Licensee any rights or license to any trademark,  trade name, certification mark, service mark, domain name, product name, logo, patent, technical information, or copyright of Licensor other  than as specified herein. All rights not specifically granted to Licensee are reserved to Licensor.

text: THIS AGREEMENT is made July 31, 2017

text: "Effective Date" means the Completion Date as defined in the Purchase Agreement.

text: "Contract Year" means the twelve (12) month period beginning on the Effective Date, and each subsequent twelve (12) month period during the Term.

text: "Term" has the meaning ascribed thereto in clause 12.1.

text: the warranties set forth in clause 7.1 will extend for a period of [Redacted - Commercially Sensitive - Warranty Details]

text: for the period set forth in clause 7.4

text: Prices are firm and fixed for the Term

text: Philips shall not be held liable for rejecting any Purchase Order through which the volume in any Contract Year or the relevant quarter exceeds the volume indicated in the Production Plan.

text: always subject to the supply limitations, if any, outlined in the Production Plan

text: Customer shall have the right to increase or decrease, as the case may be, the [Redacted- Commercially Sensitive] Forecast only within the limitations set forth in the Production Plan per quarter.
rationale: Volume Restriction rule: "only within the limitations set forth in the Production Plan" constrains customer forecast changes in the company's favor.

text: the first [Redacted - Commercially Sensitive] of each Forecast shall constitute a binding commitment of Customer to purchase the quantities of Products set forth in the relevant Forecast
rationale: Minimum Commitment rule: "shall constitute a binding commitment of Customer to purchase" secures firm demand for the company.

text: will be enforceable by Customer and its Affiliates, and their successors, assigns, subcontractors, distributors, dealers, agents and customers and all other entities combining, selling or using Products or goods into which Products have been incorporated
rationale: Third Party Beneficiary rule: "enforceable by ... all other entities combining, selling or using Products" creates broad, one-sided downstream liability.

text: shall apply in respect of Products sold or distributed on or after the Effective Date

text: Customer grants to Philips, during the Term, a non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-transferrable right to make, have made, use, sell, reproduce, adapt, distribute, or otherwise use or practice Customer's Intellectual Property Rights solely in connection with manufacturing of the Products and packaging to Customer pursuant to this Agreement.

Philips hereby assigns and shall cause its Affiliates to assign all right title and interest in New Technology to Customer

text: Philips and its Affiliates hereby grant to Customer under any such Intellectual Property Rights, which are applicable or used for the manufacturing of the Product, a non- exclusive, non-transferable (except in accordance with clause 18.4 (Assignment)), irrevocable, world-wide, fully paid-up license, without the right to grant sub-licenses, to make, have made, sell or commercialize in any other way the Product.

text: On termination or expiry of this Agreement Philips shall facilitate an orderly transition of suppliers from Philips to Customer in accordance with the requirements outlined in Section 5.4 (Material Supplier Contracts) of the Purchase Agreement
rationale: Flag rule: Philips must "facilitate an orderly transition of suppliers", an open-ended one-sided obligation on Philips.

text: Philips undertakes to sell all Products which have been ordered by Customer but not yet delivered at the date of termination upon the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

text: The limitations and exclusions set forth above in this clause 10 shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable Law.
rationale: Liability cap rule: "shall apply to the fullest extent permitted" gives no confirmed mutuality or 12-month fee floor; depends on clause 10.

text: All such charges will be charged to Customer at cost, without any additional markup.

text: Upon request of any Governmental Authority or any third party entity authorized by a Governmental Authority, such entity shall, for the purpose of regulatory review and compliance, have access to observe and inspect the: (i) facilities of Philips; and (ii) manufacturing, testing, storage and preparation for shipment of Product, including development operations in respect of manufacturing, and auditing the Philips facility for compliance with applicable Laws.

text: Philips shall give Customer prompt written notice of any upcoming inspections or audits by a Governmental Authority, governmental entity or any third party entity authorized by a Governmental Authority of the Philips facility or any of the foregoing, shall provide Customer with a written summary of such inspection or audit within five (5) Business Days following completion thereof.

text: Philips shall maintain, and provide Customer reasonable access to, all records, both during and after the termination or expiration of this Agreement, in accordance with the Quality Agreement.

text: prior to the Effective Date

text: No rights or obligations in respect of a Party's Confidential Information other than those expressly stated in this Agreement are granted to the other Party or to be implied from this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "No rights... implied" is a mutual, market-standard exclusion of implied confidentiality licenses.

text: This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party, in whole or in part, to any Third Party without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this Agreement as a whole, and all of its rights and obligations hereunder, without the consent of the other Party, but upon written notice to the other Party (a) to an Affiliate, or (b) in case of a transfer of all, or substantially all, stock or assets of such Party or the relevant business activity through which such Party acts in this Agreement to a Third Party or to any partnership or other venture in which such business activity is to participate.

text: "Effective Date" shall mean February 16, 1998.

text: "Term" shall mean the period commencing on the Effective Date and terminating on the eighth anniversary of the Commencement Date, unless the Agreement is extended in accordance with its provisions.

text: The initial term of this Agreement shall be the Term, unless extended or earlier terminated in accordance with this Agreement.

text: Customer may, at its option, renew this Agreement for one (1) twelve month period at the then-current terms and conditions of this Agreement.

text: Customer shall exercise its option, if at all, by delivering written notice to M&I at least five (5) months prior to expiration of the Term.

text: at least eighteen (18) months prior to the expiration of the Term, M&I shall submit to Customer a written proposal for renewal of this Agreement.

text: "Change in Control" shall mean any event or series of events by which (i) any person or entity or group of persons or entities shall acquire Control of another person or entity or (ii) in the case of a corporation, during any period of 12 consecutive months commencing before or after the date hereof, individuals who at the beginning of such 12-month period were directors of such corporation shall cease for any reason to constitute a majority of the board of directors of such corporation.

text: Notwithstanding any provision in the Agreement to the contrary, M&I's liability to Customer for claims arising out of the ACH Services performed by M&I pursuant to this Section 6.5 shall be limited to errors and omissions which are caused solely by M&I's gross negligence or willful misconduct and which cannot be remedied through the processing of appropriate corrected ACH Entry(ies).

text: M&I agrees to provide the licenses, products, interfaces and network management services associated with the PC Teller and Sales Partner/BankerInsight software

text: Customer agrees to use M&I primarily for Customer's Bankcard Services data processing.

text: Customer further agrees that the software used to provide the EFT services may not be available for license by Customer.

text: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in the Agreement, or any general discount specified in the Fee Schedule, the fees for Bankcard Services shall not be subject to any discounts.

text: Such discount shall not apply to any EFT service which is not a part of M&I's 1997 standard published priced list.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: discount excluded for EFT services outside the '1997 standard published priced list', an outdated benchmark.

text: all charges for Services shall be computed using M&I's then-current standard published prices, paid in advance, as determined by M&I.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: charges use 'then-current standard published prices... as determined by M&I', allowing unilateral pricing, paid in advance.

text: Customer shall be entitled to receive discounts on certain Services as specifically set forth in the marked up price list made part of the Fee Schedule.
rationale: Favorable to Customer: grants discounts 'as specifically set forth' in the marked-up price list, though scope is limited.

text: a minimum monthly fee ("Monthly Base Fee") for certain bundled data processing Services
rationale: Flag minimum commitment: 'minimum monthly fee ('Monthly Base Fee')' applies regardless of usage, creating a fixed payment obligation.

text: All minimum monthly fees (including the Monthly Base Fee) are due in advance on the first day of the calendar month in which the Services are to be performed, prorated for any partial month.
rationale: Flag minimum commitment: minimum fees 'due in advance on the first day' of each month, adding cash-flow burden.

text: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee
rationale: Termination for Convenience rule: "upon at least one (1) years' written notice" exceeds the 90-day minimum, so it complies.

text: M&I may, at any time, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services) upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Customer.
rationale: Termination rule addresses counterparty termination; here M&I gives "ninety (90) days' prior written notice," which is compliant.

text: Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
rationale: Liquidated Damages rule: "deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty" is a pre-set damages term requiring legal approval.

text: M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
rationale: Cap rule requires mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees; this caps only "M&I's total liability" at "the three (3) months prior."

text: The Termination for Convenience Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4.
rationale: Uncapped Liability rule: "Liability must be capped"; this carves the fee out of "the limitations set forth in Section 13.4."

text: Throughout the Term of this Agreement, M&I shall maintain at all times at its own cost and expense:

text: Developer shall be in default of its obligations under the Development Schedule and Franchisor shall be entitled to exercise its rights and remedies under this Agreement, up to and including termination of this Agreement.

text: If Developer fails to meet the opening date for any El Pollo Loco® Restaurant to be developed under this Agreement, Developer shall be in default

text: Franchisor will suffer lost revenues, including royalties and other fees which would be difficult to calculate
rationale: Liquidated damages rule: "would be difficult to calculate" signals pre-set damages requiring legal approval; enforceability risk.

text: Franchisor shall have no liability under any lease or purchase agreement for any El Pollo Loco® Restaurant location developed under this Agreement and shall not guarantee Developer's obligations thereunder.
rationale: Disclaimer of lease liability and no guarantee protects the company; it is not a liability cap, so no cap-rule issue arises.

text: Integra (i) shall not apply or have applied any other coating to any Integra Products treated with the PcoMed Surface Modification Technology, unless that coating is for the sole purpose of identification or sterilization

text: Integra shall use commercially reasonable efforts to Sell Treated Integra Products and Partially Treated Integra Products that generate payments to PcoMed of no less than the Minimum Payments applicable to each Minimum Payment Period.
rationale: Deviation rule: "commercially reasonable efforts to Sell" tied to "no less than the Minimum Payments" places revenue-target risk on Integra.

text: Integra shall pay PcoMed a Fee of ***% of Net Sales of all Treated Integra Product Sold by Integra or its Affiliates.
rationale: Deviation rule: "Fee of ***% of Net Sales" on all treated product; rate redacted, so economics cannot be verified.

text: Integra shall pay PcoMed a Fee of ***% of Net Sales of all Partially Treated Integra Product Sold by Integra or its Affiliates.
rationale: Deviation rule: "Fee of ***% of Net Sales" on partially treated product; rate redacted, so economics cannot be verified.

text: then Integra may offset, dollar for dollar, against Fees up to *** percent (***%) of Integra's reasonable, out-of-pocket expenses, costs, fees (including reasonable attorneys' fees), and other consideration related to the investigation, negotiation and settlement paid by Integra to such Third Party to obtain such settlement or license with respect to the PcoMed Surface Modification Technology.
rationale: Deviation rule: offset "up to *** percent" against Fees; cap redacted, limiting Integra's recovery of settlement costs.

text: After early termination of this Agreement (other than a termination based on a breach of Sections 5 or 8 by Integra) and continuing for a period of eighteen (18) months thereafter, Integra and its Affiliates may Sell any Treated Integra Product and Partially Treated Integra Product in its inventory in the Field
rationale: Deviation rule: "may Sell any Treated Integra Product... in its inventory" for 18 months favors Integra; limited one-sided burden.

text: Integra shall have no liability at any time to PcoMed for Integra's failure to pay the Minimum Payment.
