text: Payments due under Section 2.2 shall be payable to PcoMed by Integra on a quarterly basis within 45 days following the end of each calendar quarter.
rationale: Rule flags deviations from market practice; quarterly payment within "45 days" is a standard, market-typical payment term.

text: Such records and documentation will be available for inspection during such period by an independent certified public accountant selected by PcoMed and reasonably acceptable to Integra, solely for the purpose of verifying the payments made by Integra under this Agreement.

text: Such inspections shall be made no more than once each calendar year during ordinary business hours and on reasonable prior notice and shall be at PcoMed's sole cost and expense.
rationale: Rule flags one-sided obligations; "no more than once each calendar year" and "at PcoMed's sole cost" favor Integra.

text: (e) Non-Compete. The Settlement Agreement and Mutual Release between *** and *** does not contain a covenant-non-compete applicable to *** and, to the best of PcoMed's current knowledge, *** is not subject to any covenant-non-compete that would prevent is employment with PcoMed.

text: Integra hereby represents and warrants to PcoMed as follows:

text: Integra is the sole holder of all legal and equitable right, title and interest in and to the Integra Technology.
rationale: Integra's sole ownership of its own technology; no PcoMed IP is assigned to the counterparty.

text: Integra currently holds valid and effective assignments of all inventors' rights to all the inventions covered by the Integra Technology.
rationale: Confirms Integra's own inventor assignments; PcoMed intellectual property is not transferred to Integra.

text: All PcoMed Technology shall remain the property of PcoMed, and all Integra Technology shall remain the property of Integra. Any Invention that is neither PcoMed Technology nor Integra Technology but that is Derived during the Term jointly by the parties relating to this Agreement shall be the property of (i) PcoMed if it relates primarily to the PcoMed Technology and (ii) Integra if it relates primarily to the Integra Products;
rationale: Ownership of jointly Derived inventions turns on whether they relate "primarily" to a technology, which is ambiguous.

text: Except with regard to the foregoing joint Inventions or methods, each party hereby assigns to the other, by way of present and future assignment, all of the right, title and interest (including all Intellectual Property Rights therein) that it has or may have in any such Invention that is jointly Derived and that is subject to ownership by the other party.
rationale: Rule bars assigning company IP to counterparty; "each party hereby assigns to the other" directly breaches it.

text: All Inventions and Intellectual Property Rights that relate primarily to the PcoMed Technology Derived during the Term of this Agreement shall remain as the sole and exclusive property of PcoMed.
rationale: PcoMed-related inventions "shall remain as the sole and exclusive property of PcoMed"; company IP is retained.

text: PcoMed shall at all times, at its sole election and expense, have the exclusive and sole right to file patent applications covering the PcoMed Surface Modification Technology in its own name.
rationale: Exclusive patent filing right "sole election" is an exclusive arrangement needing business and legal approval.

text: NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

text: NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, NOTHING IN THIS SECTION IS INTENDED TO LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR BREACHES OF SECTION 3.1 (GRANT OF RIGHTS), SECTION 5 (CONFIDENTIALITY PROVISIONS), OR SECTIONS 8.1 AND 8.2 (OWNERSHIP AND LICENSE).

text: Any and all of Integra's reasonable expenses, costs and fees (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Integra in the investigation, commencement, pursuit, enforcement, defense and settlement of any infringement related exclusively to the PcoMed Surface Modification Technology that are not reimbursed as provided above, shall be fully creditable, dollar for dollar, against the Minimum Payments or Fees that would otherwise be due and owing hereunder.

rationale: Rule: flag deviations from market practice. "governed by ... the laws of the State of New York" is a neutral, market-standard choice.

text: All actions arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be heard and determined exclusively in any New York state or federal court sitting in the Borough of Manhattan of The City of New York.

text: This Agreement may not be assigned by any party or by operation of law or otherwise without the prior written consent of each of the other parties. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section shall be null and void.

text: Nothing set forth in this Agreement shall confer or give or shall be construed to confer or give to any party other than the Parties any rights or remedies against any Person other than as expressly set forth herein.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "confer or give to any party other than the Parties" is a mutual, standard no-third-party-beneficiary clause.

text: No party shall be entitled to recover lost profits or benefit of the bargain damages.

text: "Effective Date" shall mean the date on which the Parties sign and execute this Agreement .

text: IMPCO has the right to grant licenses to MINDA-IMPCO LTD. during the term of this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "IMPCO has the right to grant licenses" is one-directional, with no defined scope or exclusivity.

text: After the expiry of the five (5) year period, if a Party intends to sell any or all of its shares of the JVC (the "Transferor"), it shall first make an offer by a written notice to the other Parties (the "Transferee") to purchase such shares and the other Parties shall have the right to purchase the offered shares in proportion of their existing shareholding.
rationale: Mutual pro-rata right of first offer after five years, a market-standard term; "in proportion of their existing shareholding" keeps it balanced.

text: If no Transferee accepts to purchase the shares offered by the Transferor, in whole or in part, the Transferor may sell such shares to a third party on terms and conditions no more favourable than those offered to the Transferees, including the price of the shares.
rationale: Standard ROFR tail allowing third-party sale "no more favourable" than offered terms; mutual and market-typical.

text: Each party hereto agrees not to transfer, sell, pledge, mortgage or make other disposition (whether by way of fixed or floating charge) or encumbrance on its shares in the JVC except as otherwise provided in this Agreement and/or except by consent of the Parties to this Agreement and in the manner laid out in the M&A.
rationale: Transfer and encumbrance bar "except by consent of the Parties" matches the rule requiring consent of both parties.

text: No party hereto may transfer its shares in the JVC for a period of five (5) years from the date of allotment except as provided above.
rationale: Five-year transfer lock-up "except as provided above" lacks the playbook's written-consent carve-out, restricting exit without consent.

text: Any transfer of the shares of the JVC to a third party shall be subject to the full unconditional assumption in writing by such third party of all obligations of the Transferor as provided in Article 6.4.
rationale: "full unconditional assumption in writing" of obligations protects the company against transferee liability gaps.

text: The third party shall not have a conflict of interest and should not be strategically incompatible to the other Parties to the Agreement.
rationale: "strategically incompatible" is vague and subjective, creating uncertainty beyond the playbook's consent-based assignment rule.

text: IMPCO and MIL/MINDA may transfer any of its holdings in the JVC to an Affiliate, without requiring the consent of the other Parties, provided that, such an Affiliate shall also be bound by the provisions of this Agreement and shall execute a deed of adherence as mentioned above.
rationale: "without requiring the consent of the other Parties" to Affiliates departs from the rule, though deed of adherence mitigates.

text: The Parties agree that the shares held by them shall not be pledged to a third party or otherwise encumbered during the term of this Agreement.
rationale: Absolute bar on pledging or encumbering shares "during the term" has no consent exception, departing from the playbook.

text: Such shares shall be transferred at a price which shall be the price indicated in the offer notice to the extent the same is in accordance with, the regulations of the Securities and Exchange Board of India or the Reserve Bank of India, if applicable.
rationale: Pricing tied to SEBI/RBI regulations "if applicable" is a compliance-based, market-standard mechanism.

text: The JVC will be permitted to use the following words in Products which are manufactured by MINDA IMPCO Limited.
rationale: Trademark use permitted without stated scope, duration, quality control, or royalty terms, creating one-sided licensing exposure.

text: Subject to the provisions of this Agreement, all products, will carry the trademark of MINDA IMPCO.
rationale: "all products, will carry the trademark" imposes a broad branding obligation on the JVC without limits or reciprocal terms.

text: The M&A shall be in accordance with the law for the time being in force in India.
rationale: Governing law "in accordance with the law for the time being in force in India" is standard and neutral.

text: Successors & Assigns: All provisions of this Agreement shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon the respective successors, representatives, heirs and permitted assigns of the Parties hereto.
rationale: Standard successors clause; "permitted assigns" presupposes the consent rule, so it does not itself permit assignment.

text: IMPCO expressly agrees that during the existence of this Agreement, IMPCO shall not enter into any other Joint Venture Agreement or Marketing/Distribution Agreement, with any company or person(s) in the Territory with respect to the Products.
rationale: Exclusivity rule needs approval; "shall not enter into any other Joint Venture Agreement" restricts IMPCO's business in the Territory.

text: during the term of the Agreement, and thereafter for a period of five (5) years after the termination of the Agreement (such termination being termination by IMPCO due to default by MINDA/MIL), MIL/MINDA shall not, directly or indirectly, either alone or collectively or through any of its associates, affiliates, including subsidiaries or any entity owned or controlled by it enter into another joint venture agreement or marketing/distribution agreement with any company or persons in respect
rationale: Non-compete rule needs approval; "thereafter for a period of five (5) years" binds MIL/MINDA and affiliates post-termination.

text: the damages that would be suffered by IMPCO as a result of breach of the provisions of this Article may not be calculable and that an award of a monetary judgment for such a breach would be an inadequate remedy.
rationale: Non-compete rule needs approval; "an award of a monetary judgment... would be an inadequate remedy" concedes injunctive relief against the company.

text: the duration for which the covenants in this Article are to be effective is reasonable. In the event that any court finally determines that the time period or the geographic scope of any such covenant is unreasonable or excessive and any covenant is to that extent made unenforceable
rationale: Non-compete rule needs approval; "the duration... is reasonable" and court-reformation language leave covenants enforceable at scope.

text: This Agreement shall become effective on the date of execution
rationale: Effective on "the date of execution" is conventional and mutual; no one-sided obligation evident.

text: shall continue in force and effect for an indefinite term thereafter unless terminated pursuant to the provisions of Article 16 or by all the Parties in writing.
rationale: Deviates from market practice; "an indefinite term thereafter" with exit only by Article 16 or all-party writing.

text: If the JVC fails to sell [one million dollars (US$ 1,000,000.00)] worth of Products in the Territory within [eighteen (18)] months from the date of execution of this Agreement, both the Parties will mutually discuss whether to continue or terminate the Agreement.
rationale: Minimum sales target is non-binding; "both the Parties will mutually discuss" whether to continue or terminate.

text: During reasonable business hours IMPCO and MIL/MINDA will have the right to inspect, and make copies of any and all of the JVC 's business records, including but not limited to financial records, books, accounts and reports.
rationale: Mutual inspection of JVC records; "IMPCO and MIL/MINDA will have the right" applies equally, during reasonable hours.

text: During reasonable business hours IMPCO and MIL/MINDA will have the right to visit, enter and inspect each plant and other establishment at which the JVC manufactures and/or processes the Products.
rationale: Mutual plant inspection rights limited to "reasonable business hours"; balanced and conventional.

text: the JVC will submit to IMPCO and MIL/MINDA the annual financial statement including Balance Sheets and Profit and Loss account, related Auditors Reports for such year.
rationale: Annual audited financials owed by JVC to both parties; standard reporting, not one-sided against the company.

text: MINDA IMPCO Limited has agreed to allow the JVC, the right to use the two trade marks in respect of the products, the first being under the name of "IMPCO" and the second being in the name of "MINDA IMPCO".
rationale: Trademark licence to JVC deviates from one-sided practice; no quality control or termination reversion stated, risking brand dilution.

text: the JVC will have a right to continue to use the Technical Know How already received and absorbed on the condition that royalty payments under the TAA have been paid by the JVC to IMPCO or will be paid, as the case may be, for a minimum period of five (5) years, as provided in the TAA.
rationale: Know-how survival tied to royalties "for a minimum period of five (5) years" creates lasting obligations beyond the Agreement.

text: the JVC will be allowed to use the Technical Know How to the extent the same is necessary for the purpose of implementing any orders pending in favour of its customers.
rationale: Know-how use is narrow, "necessary for the purpose of implementing any orders pending", limiting exposure.

text: the non-defaulting Party at its option, shall be entitled to sell all the shares owned by it in the JVC to the defaulting Party at the price determined in accordance with Article 15.3 below.
rationale: Change-of-control rule needs approval; forced share sale to defaulting party at "price determined in accordance with Article 15.3" could be triggered.

text: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India and the Delhi Courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any legal proceedings in respect of this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. "Delhi Courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction" puts disputes in one party's home forum, unfavorable to the US counterparty.

text: IMPCO represents and warrants that it is a company duly incorporated and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware USA with an office and legal address at 16804 Gridley Place, Cerritos, California 90703 USA
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. Standard incorporation and good-standing representation by IMPCO alone; ordinary and low exposure.

text: That MIL is a company limited by Shares, duly incorporated and existing under the laws of India.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "duly incorporated and existing under the laws of India" is a standard entity representation.

text: MINDA and MIL, hereby represent and warrant to IMPCO as follows:
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "MINDA and MIL, hereby represent and warrant to IMPCO" places warranty burden only on the Indian parties.

text: which will result in any liability on its part after the Effective Date.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "any liability on its part after the Effective Date" is ambiguous on scope and allocation of post-effective liability.

text: In the event of termination of this Agreement and consequent winding up of the JVC, the Parties agree to cooperate with each other for adequate discharge and fulfillment of the JVC's liabilities, commitments and obligations as may be necessary.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. Open-ended duty to cooperate "as may be necessary" for JVC liabilities has no defined limit or cost cap.

text: This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the state where a suit is properly filed under the terms of this paragraph, being either Illinois or New York, and without giving effect to conflict of law principles.

text: Neither party may assign the Agreement without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, except that either party may assign the Agreement without obtaining the consent of the other party to an affiliate or successor by way of purchase, merger, consolidation or similar transaction, subject to the requirement that the Agreement shall be binding and enforceable against any successor or assign.

rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. Broad sponsor indemnity favors company, but text is garbled ("from against") and truncated ("incurred as a result of").

text: Beginning on the date you begin operations under this Agreement, which is agreed to be the date set out in the Declarations Page (the "Commencement Date"), we will remit to you Net Revenues on a monthly basis.

text: 3.4 Manual. text: You agree to establish the Franchised Business and have it open and in operation within six (6) months after the Effective Date of this Agreement.

text: You agree to buy all products, equipment, furniture, supplies, materials and other products used or offered for sale at the Franchised Business only from suppliers as to whom we have given you our prior written approval (and whom we have not subsequently disapproved).
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "only from suppliers as to whom we have given you our prior written approval" creates exclusive sourcing, requiring business and legal sign-off.

text: You assign to us or our designee all of your right, title and interest in and to any and all such Allowances and authorize us (or our designee) to collect and retain any or all such Allowances without restriction.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "assign to us... all of your right, title and interest" and collect "without restriction" creates a one-sided obligation.

text: We have the right to collect and retain all manufacturing allowances, marketing allowances, rebates, contingencies, credits, monies, payments or benefits (collectively, "Allowances") offered by suppliers to you or to us (or our affiliates) based upon your purchases of Products and other goods and services.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: "We have the right to collect and retain all" supplier Allowances, including those offered to you, is one-sided.

text: With regard to insurance products offered by you, the insurance carriers will set the policy prices, and we will set the Agency Fees.
rationale: Flag pricing terms that deviate from market practice: "we will set the Agency Fees" while carriers set policy prices, a one-sided pricing split.

text: we have the right to appoint only one supplier for Approved Products and Services (which may be us or one of our affiliates)
rationale: Exclusivity needs approval: "appoint only one supplier for Approved Products" is exclusive and needs business and legal sign-off.

text: we may limit the number of approved suppliers with whom you may deal, designate sources that you must use for some or all Products and other products and services
rationale: Exclusivity needs approval: "limit the number of approved suppliers" and "designate sources" restricts supply and needs business and legal review.

text: that deviation will become our property.
rationale: IP rule not triggered as stated: "that deviation will become our property" moves IP to the company, not to the counterparty.

text: We have the right to require that our representatives be permitted to inspect the supplier's facilities, and that samples from the supplier be delivered to us.
rationale: Audit rights: "inspect the supplier's facilities" and "samples... delivered to us" are common supplier-quality terms, not clearly off-market.

text: We also reserve the right, at our option, to periodically re-inspect the facilities and products of any such approved supplier and to revoke our approval if the supplier does not continue to meet any of our then-current criteria.
rationale: Audit rights: "at our option" re-inspection and revocation favors the company; the supplier's burden is typical for approved-supplier programs.

text: a license agreement in the form that we may require (which may include a royalty fee for the right to use our Proprietary Marks and any other proprietary rights, recipes, and/or formulae)
rationale: License grant: "in the form that we may require" and royalty for "our Proprietary Marks" favors the company as licensor.

text: we may require Remodeling more often if Remodeling is required as a pre- condition to renewal (as described in Section 2.2.2 above)
rationale: Renewal term: "Remodeling more often" as a renewal pre-condition burdens the franchisee; company-favorable, with limited direct risk to us.

text: You agree that we may set reasonable restrictions on the maximum and minimum prices you may charge for the Approved Products and Services offered and sold at the Franchised Business under this Agreement.
rationale: Price Restrictions rule: "reasonable restrictions on the maximum and minimum prices" favors the company as franchisor; market-standard.

text: (a) if we have set a maximum price for a particular item, then you may charge any price for that item up to and including the maximum price we have set; and (b) if we have set a minimum price for a particular item, then you may charge any price for that item that is equal to or above the minimum price we have set.
rationale: Price Restrictions rule: "you may charge any price... up to and including the maximum price" is bounded, company-protective price control.

text: will be deemed to be our sole and exclusive property and works made-for- hire for us.
rationale: IP Ownership rule: "our sole and exclusive property" keeps work product with the company, not assigned away.

text: You hereby grant to us (and agree to obtain from your affiliates, owners, employees, and/or contractors), a perpetual, non-exclusive, and worldwide right to use any such ideas, concepts, methods, techniques and products in any businesses that we and/or our affiliates, franchisees and designees operate.
rationale: License Grant rule: "perpetual, non-exclusive, and worldwide right" runs to the company, so it benefits the company.

text: The right and license of the Proprietary Marks that we have granted to you under this Agreement is non-exclusive, and we therefore have the right, among other things:
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "is non-exclusive" means no exclusive grant to the franchisee requires approval.

text: To grant other licenses for the Proprietary Marks, in addition to licenses we may have already granted to existing franchisees;
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "To grant other licenses" confirms non-exclusivity; company keeps flexibility, no exclusive arrangement.

text: Your use of the Proprietary Marks does not give you any ownership interest or other interest in or to the Proprietary Marks, except the license granted by this Agreement.
rationale: License Grant rule: "does not give you any ownership interest" preserves company ownership of Proprietary Marks.

text: We own all right, title, and interest in and to the Proprietary Marks and the goodwill associated with and symbolized by them.
rationale: IP Ownership rule: "We own all right, title, and interest" in marks and goodwill; company retains IP.

text: Any and all goodwill arising from your use of the Proprietary Marks will inure solely and exclusively to our benefit
rationale: IP Ownership rule: "inure solely and exclusively to our benefit" keeps goodwill with the company.

text: (b) maintain stop transfer instructions on your records against the transfer of any equity securities and will only issue securities upon the face of which a legend, in a form satisfactory to us, appears which references the transfer restrictions imposed by this Agreement;
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: "stop transfer instructions" restricts franchisee transfers, protecting company; no company IP assigned.

text: (d) consistent with the transfer restrictions set out in this Agreement, maintain instructions against the transfer of any partnership interests without our prior written approval.
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: "without our prior written approval" gives company control over transfers; favorable to company.

text: (d) maintain stop transfer instructions on your records against the transfer of equity securities and will only issue securities upon the face of which bear a legend, in a form satisfactory to us, which references the transfer restrictions imposed by this Agreement.
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: "stop transfer instructions" and legend restrict franchisee equity transfers, protecting company.

text: (a) confine your activities, and your governing documents will at all times provide that your activities are confined, exclusively to operating the Franchised Business;
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "confine your activities... exclusively to operating the Franchised Business" binds franchisee, not company exclusivity.

text: covenant concerning confidentiality and competition, in the form attached as Exhibit B
rationale: Non-Compete rule: "in the form attached as Exhibit B" incorporates unreviewed covenant terms; content must be checked for company restrictions.

text: To use the Proprietary Marks ourselves in connection with selling Services and products
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "To use the Proprietary Marks ourselves" is a reserved company right, not an exclusive grant.

text: To develop and establish other systems using the same or similar Proprietary Marks, or any other proprietary marks, and to grant licenses or franchises for those other marks without giving you any rights to those other marks.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "grant licenses or franchises for those other marks" preserves company freedom; no exclusivity is conferred.

text: We will lend to you (or permit you to have access to) one (1) copy of our Manual, only for the term of this Agreement, and only for your use in connection with operating the Franchised Business during the term of this Agreement.
rationale: One-sided obligations rule: "only for the term of this Agreement" limits the manual loan and protects company.

text: The Manual will at all times remain our sole property and you agree to promptly return the Manual when this Agreement expires or if it is terminated.
rationale: IP assignment rule: "will at all times remain our sole property" keeps the Manual with the company.

text: designate us as a third party beneficiary of such covenants with the independent right to enforce them
rationale: Market practice rule: "independent right to enforce them" strengthens company's ability to enforce covenants.

text: for review or auditing, such other forms, reports, records, information, and data as and when we may reasonably designate
rationale: Audit rule: "as and when we may reasonably designate" favors company; reasonableness qualifier limits overreach.

text: we will have full access to the data and information that you provide to the accounting service provider or through the designated program
rationale: Audit rule: "full access to the data" benefits company; no company-side obligation or exposure is created.

text: You agree that if do not submit those reports to us in a timely manner, we will have the right to charge you for the costs that we incur in auditing your records.
rationale: Audit rule: "we will have the right to charge you" shifts audit costs to franchisee, favoring company.

text: You agree that upon our request, and for a limited period of time, you will provide us (and/or our agents, such as our auditors) with passwords and pass codes necessary for the limited purpose of accessing your computer system in order to conduct the inspections specified in this Section 12.
rationale: Audit rule: "passwords and pass codes" to "your computer system" creates company data security and privacy exposure.

text: We have the right at all reasonable times to examine, copy, and/or personally review or audit (at our expense) all of your sales receipts, books, records, and sales and income tax returns in person or through electronic access (at our option).
rationale: Audit rule: "(at our expense)" limits company cost; reasonable-times access is standard for franchisors.

text: We will also have the right, at any time, to have an independent audit made of your books and records.
rationale: Audit rule: "at any time" independent audit with no stated cost allocation, unlike the "at our expense" clause.

text: If we conduct an inspection because you did not timely provide sales reports to us, or if an inspection discloses that you understated your sales, in any report to us (and/or underpaid your royalties), by three percent (3%) or more, or if you did not maintain and/or provide us with access to your records, then you agree (in addition to paying us the overdue amount and interest) to reimburse us for any and all costs and expenses we incur in connection with the inspection (including travel, lodging and wages expenses, and reasonable accounting and legal costs).
rationale: Audit rule flags one-sided terms; "reimburse us for any and all costs" shifts inspection costs onto you at a 3% threshold.

text: If an inspection should reveal that you have understated any payments in any report to us, then this will constitute a default under this Agreement, and you agree to immediately pay us the amount understated upon demand, in addition to interest from the date such amount was due until paid
rationale: Audit rule flags one-sided terms; any understatement "will constitute a default" with immediate payment "upon demand" plus interest.

text: 12.5 Operational Inspections. In addition to the provisions of Section 12.5 above, you also grant to us and our agents the right to enter upon the Franchised Business premises at any reasonable time for the purpose of conducting inspections, for among other purposes, preserving the validity of the Proprietary Marks, and verifying your compliance with this Agreement and the policies and procedures outlined in the Manual.
rationale: Audit rule flags one-sided terms; "at any reasonable time" inspection access is a common, market-standard franchisor right.

text: For each Month during the term of this Agreement, you agree to contribute an amount up to two percent (2%) of Gross Revenues to be allocated in the manner described in Section 13.2 below (the "Marketing Contribution").
rationale: Revenue rule flags one-sided terms; a "up to two percent (2%)" marketing contribution is typical franchise practice.

text: A majority of the Goosehead Business owners in the Regional Fund may vote to increase the amount of each Goosehead Business owner's contribution to the Regional Fund by up to an additional two percent (2%) of each Goosehead Business's Gross Revenues.
rationale: Revenue rule flags one-sided terms; majority vote can raise contributions "by up to an additional two percent (2%)", binding minority owners.

text: You acknowledge and agree that any and all copyright in and to advertising, marketing materials, and promotional plans developed by or on behalf of you will be our sole property, and you agree to sign such documents
rationale: IP rule covers company IP going to counterparty; here franchisee materials become "our sole property," which favors the company.

text: You agree that all data that you collect, create, provide, or otherwise develop on your Computer System (whether or not uploaded to our system from your system and/or downloaded from your system to our system) is and will be owned exclusively by us, and that we will have the right to access, download, and use that data in any manner that we deem appropriate without compensation to you.
rationale: Ip Ownership Assignment rule: company data is 'owned exclusively by us' with no compensation, so company IP passes to counterparty.

text: You agree that all other data that you create or collect in connection with the System, and in connection with your operation of the Franchised Business (including customer lists and transaction data), is and will be owned exclusively by us during the term of, and after termination or expiration of, this Agreement.
rationale: Ip Ownership Assignment rule: customer lists and transaction data are 'owned exclusively by us' during and after the term, assigning company IP away.

text: In order to operate your Franchised Business under this Agreement, we hereby license use of such data back to you, at no additional cost, solely for the term of this Agreement and for your use in connection with operating the Franchised Business.
rationale: License Grant rule: company gets back only a term-limited license to its own data, 'solely for the term of this Agreement.'

text: You agree to afford us unimpeded access to your Computer System and Required Software, including all information and data maintained thereon, in the manner, form, and at the times that we request.
rationale: Audit Rights rule: 'unimpeded access' to systems and data 'at the times that we request' is one-sided and exceeds market practice.

text: You agree to transfer to us all data (in the digital machine-readable format that we specify, and/or printed copies, and/or originals) promptly upon our request when made, whether periodically during the term of this Agreement, upon termination and/or expiration of this Agreement, any transfer of an interest in you, and/or a transfer of the Franchised Business.
rationale: Change Of Control rule: data transfer is triggered by 'any transfer of an interest in you,' a change-of-control event needing approval.

text: you agree to procure and maintain in full force and effect during the term of this Agreement
rationale: Insurance rule: "procure and maintain in full force and effect" is standard market language for ongoing coverage.

text: Commercial general liability insurance, including us, and any entity in which we have an interest and any entity affiliated with us
rationale: Insurance rule: "any entity in which we have an interest" extends additional-insured scope beyond market practice.

text: Professional indemnity insurance providing coverage for loss or damage arising out of an act or omission of the franchisee or its employees
rationale: Insurance rule: professional indemnity limited to franchisee's own acts or omissions is standard market practice.

text: Business automobile liability insurance, including owned, non-owned and hired car coverage
rationale: Insurance rule: "owned, non-owned and hired" auto liability is standard market coverage.

text: Statutory workers' compensation insurance and employer's liability insurance for a minimum limit
rationale: Insurance rule: statutory workers' compensation and employer's liability is standard, expected coverage.

text: Data theft and cybersecurity coverage.
rationale: Insurance rule: "Data theft and cybersecurity coverage" has no stated limits, leaving scope and cost open-ended.

text: Commercial umbrella liability insurance with limits which bring the total of all primary underlying coverages
rationale: Insurance rule: umbrella liability sized to total primary coverage is standard market practice.

text: Property insurance providing coverage for direct physical loss or damage to real and personal property for all risk perils
rationale: Insurance rule: all-risk property coverage for direct physical loss is standard market practice.

text: you must also obtain flood insurance coverage in the amount of the lesser of 90% of the replacement cost or the maximum coverage available from the National Flood Insurance Program
rationale: Insurance rule: "lesser of 90% of the replacement cost" flood limit is a specific, somewhat unusual requirement to verify.

text: In the event of cancellation, material change, or non-renewal of any policy, sixty (60) days' advance written notice must be provided to us
rationale: Insurance rule: "sixty (60) days' advance written notice" to us on cancellation is a common carrier-notice term.

text: All policies must waive subrogation as between us (and our insurance carriers) and you (and your insurance carriers).
rationale: Insurance rule: "waive subrogation as between us ... and you" is mutual, so not one-sided.

text: you agree to deliver to us certificates of insurance evidencing the proper coverage with limits not less than those required under this Agreement
rationale: Insurance rule: delivering certificates evidencing required coverage is routine and expected.

text: All public liability and property damage policies except workers' compensation must list us as an additional named insured
rationale: Insurance rule: "additional named insured" on liability policies is standard market practice.

text: You acknowledge and agree that the specifications and coverage requirements in this Section 15 are minimums
rationale: Insurance rule: "coverage requirements ... are minimums" is open-ended and one-sided, allowing unilateral escalation.

text: on the first anniversary of the Effective Date, and on each subsequent anniversary of the Effective Date, you agree to provide us with proof of insurance
rationale: Insurance rule: annual "proof of insurance" on anniversaries is routine compliance.

text: on the first anniversary of the Effective Date, and on each subsequent anniversary of the Effective Date
rationale: Insurance rule: anniversary of Effective Date is only a timing reference, not a risk term.

text: We will have the right to transfer or assign this Agreement and all or any part of our rights or obligations under this Agreement to any person or legal entity
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: "right to transfer or assign ... to any person" lets us assign without mutual consent.

text: you agree not to permit the identity of those owners, or their respective interests in you, to change without complying with this Agreement
rationale: Change of control rule: owner identity may not "change without complying with this Agreement," triggering counterparty control rights.

text: We will have a continuing right to designate any person or entity that owns a direct or indirect interest in you as a Principal
rationale: Change of control rule: "continuing right to designate any person ... as a Principal" is one-sided control over ownership.

text: You agree not to make a transfer (and not to permit any other party to make a transfer) without our prior written consent.
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: only "our prior written consent" is required, not mutual consent of both parties.

text: the term "transfer" is agreed to mean any sale, assignment, conveyance, pledge, encumbrance, merger, creation of a security interest in, and/or giving away of any direct or indirect interest in
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: "transfer" broadly covers pledge, encumbrance and merger, expanding restrictions beyond market norms.

text: Any purported assignment or transfer not having our prior written consent as required by this Section 16 will be null and void
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: non-consented transfer "will be null and void" is a harsh, one-sided remedy.

text: you will not issue any voting securities or interests, or securities or interests convertible into voting securities
rationale: Change of control rule: "will not issue any voting securities" restricts equity changes without mutual consent mechanics.

text: the partners of that partnership will not, without our prior written consent, admit additional general partners, remove a general partner, or otherwise materially alter the powers of any general partner
rationale: Change of control rule: partner changes need "our prior written consent", giving counterparty control over ownership.

text: Principals must not, without our prior written consent, transfer, pledge, and/or otherwise encumber their interest in you.
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: Principals may not "transfer, pledge" interests without our consent, one-sided restriction.

text: We will not unreasonably withhold any consent required by Section 16.4 above
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: "will not unreasonably withhold any consent" is a reasonableness standard favoring the company.

text: The transferor must have executed a general release, in a form satisfactory to us, of any and all claims against us and our affiliates, successors, and assigns
rationale: Anti-assignment rule: general release "in a form satisfactory to us" is one-sided and gives us discretion.

text: The transferee of a Principal will be designated as a Principal and each transferee who is designated a Principal must enter into a written agreement
rationale: Change of control rule: transferee "will be designated as a Principal" imposes our designation and agreement requirements.

text: The transfer fee will be in an amount equal to fifteen percent (15%) of your Initial Franchise Fee if you complete a transfer (as defined in this Section) to another franchisee currently operating within the System
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. A 15% fee on transfer to a franchisee is a cost, not a consent term.

text: 16.8 No Transfers to a Non-Franchisee Party to Operate a Similar Business. You agree that neither you nor any Principal of yours will transfer or attempt to transfer any or all of your Franchised Business to a third party who will operate a similar business at the Approved Location but not under the System and the Proprietary Marks, and not under a franchise agreement with us.
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. Bars transfers to outside operators of similar business, protecting the company.

text: If the transfer involves the sale of all or any part of your book of insurance business (including Commissions payable in connection with that business), then upon completion of the transfer this Agreement shall terminate
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: mutual consent required. 'this Agreement shall terminate' upon transfer is automatic and one-sided.

text: The executor, administrator, or personal representative of such person will transfer such interest to a third party approved by us within six (6) months after such death or mental incapacity.
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. 'third party approved by us' keeps company approval over transferee.

text: we will have the option, but not the obligation, to purchase your interest in the Franchised Business
rationale: ROFR rule: flag one-sided terms. 'option, but not the obligation' favors the company and imposes no duty on it.

text: it is the parties' understanding and agreement that any transfer of you, your obligations, and/or rights under this Agreement
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. Clause is truncated and its operative consent mechanism is unclear.

text: The transferor must acknowledge and agree that the transferor will remain bound by the covenants contained in Sections 19.3 - 19.5 below.
rationale: Non-Compete rule: restrictions on company activity need approval. This binds the transferor, not the company.

text: The transferor must remain liable for all of the obligations to us in connection with the Franchised Business that arose before the effective date of the transfer
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. 'transferor must remain liable' protects the company's accrued claims.

text: We will have the right to require that the transferee execute, for a term ending on the expiration date of this Agreement, the form of franchise agreement that we are then offering to new System franchisees
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. Forcing transferee to sign current franchise form may alter agreed terms.

text: it is agreed that any such offering will be subject to our approval as to the structure and voting control of the offeror (and you, if you are not the offeror) after the financing is completed.
rationale: Change Of Control rule: counterparty approval needed. 'subject to our approval as to... voting control' gives company control rights.

text: agreeing to be bound as a Principal under the terms of this Agreement as long as such person or entity owns any interest in you
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule: consent required. Principals bound 'as long as' they own interest, favoring the company.

text: We will then have the prior right and option, to be exercised by notice given at any time before the effective date of such proposed assignment and assumption, to accept an assignment of the Agreement to us upon the same terms and conditions, and for the same consideration, if any, as in the bona fide offer made by the proposed assignee
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "prior right and option" lets franchisor take over any deal, a one-sided right with no reciprocity.

text: If you or any of your Principals purport to transfer any rights or obligations under this Agreement or any interest to any third party in a manner that is contrary to the terms of Section 16 above
rationale: Rule: assignment requires both parties' consent. Clause restricts only "you or any of your Principals" transfers, so it is one-sided.

text: If an approved transfer of an interest in you is not completed within a reasonable time, as required by Sections 16.7 above
rationale: Rule: counterparty termination on change of control needs approval. "is not completed within a reasonable time" creates a termination trigger.

text: and the Agreement is assumed, or assignment of the same to any person or entity who has made a bona fide offer to accept an assignment of the Agreement is contemplated, pursuant to the U.S. Bankruptcy Code
rationale: Rule: assignment requires both parties' consent. "U.S. Bankruptcy Code" reference is standard statutory language, a minor deviation.

text: We will have the right (but not the obligation) to require you to assign to us any interest that you (and/or your affiliates) may have in the lease or sublease for the ground upon which the Franchised Business is operated and/or for the building in which the Franchised Business is operated.
rationale: Rule: assignment requires both parties' consent. "right (but not the obligation) to require you to assign" forces transfer of lease interests unilaterally.

text: You agree that you will pay us all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees, court costs, discovery costs, and all other related expenses), that we incur as a result of any default by you under this Agreement and any other agreement between the parties (and their respective affiliates) (in addition to other remedies that we may have).
rationale: Rule: liability must be capped. "pay us all damages, costs, and expenses" is uncapped and needs legal approval.

text: Within thirty (30) days after expiration or non-renewal under this Agreement and/or default under your lease/sublease for the premises, we shall buy from you (and/or your affiliates) all assets of the Franchised Business.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "we shall buy from you... all assets" imposes a mandatory buyback, even on default.

text: Covenant Not to Compete or Engage in Injurious Conduct. Accordingly, you covenant and agree that, during the term of this Agreement and for a continuous period of two (2) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, and/or a transfer as contemplated in Section 16 above, you will not directly, indirectly, for yourself, or through, on behalf of, or in conjunction with any party, in any manner whatsoever, do any of the following:
rationale: Rule covers restrictions on company activity; "you will not directly, indirectly" restricts the franchisee, not the company.

text: Divert or attempt to divert any actual or potential business or customer of any Goosehead Business to any competitor or otherwise take any action injurious or prejudicial to the goodwill associated with the Marks and the System.
rationale: One-sided protection for company; "Divert or attempt to divert" is standard non-solicit language, though "any action injurious" is broad.

text: Employ or seek to employ any person who is then employed by us or any other Goosehead Business franchisee or developer, or otherwise directly or indirectly induce such person to leave his or her employment.
rationale: Protects company's workforce; "Employ or seek to employ" restricts franchisee only, not company activity.

text: Own, maintain, develop, operate, engage in, franchise or license, make loans to, lease real or personal property to, be associated with, accept any compensation or remuneration from, and/or have any whatsoever interest in, or render services or give advice to, any Competitive Business.
rationale: Rule: company activity restrictions need approval. "any whatsoever interest" and "render services or give advice" are overbroad and may be unenforceable.

text: As used in this Section 19, the term "Competitive Business" is agreed to mean any property and/or casualty insurance distribution business.
rationale: Defining "any property and/or casualty insurance distribution business" as competitive is very broad, creating enforceability risk for the company.

text: During the two-year period following the expiration, the non- renewal, or earlier termination of this Agreement, or a transfer as contemplated under Section 16 above, these restrictions will apply only within the city and county in which the Approved Location is situated.
rationale: "only within the city and county" narrows the company's protection against competing franchisee activity beyond that area.

text: These restrictions will not apply to businesses that you operate that we (or our affiliates) have franchised to you pursuant to a valid franchise agreement.
rationale: Carve-out for franchisee's own franchised businesses; "will not apply" does not restrict company activity and is market-typical.

text: You further covenant and agree that, for a continuous period of two (2) years after (1) the expiration of this Agreement, (2) the non-renewal of this Agreement, (3) the termination of this Agreement, and/or (4) a transfer as contemplated in Section 16 above:
rationale: Two-year post-term duration restricts franchisee; "for a continuous period of two (2) years" is within typical market practice.

text: you will not directly or indirectly, for yourself, or through, on behalf of, or in conjunction with any person, firm, partnership, corporation, or other entity, sell, assign, lease, and/or transfer the Approved Location to any person, firm, partnership, corporation, or other entity that you know, or have reason to know, intends to operate a Competitive Business at the Approved Location; and
rationale: Restricts franchisee transfers to competitors; "that you know, or have reason to know" protects company interests.

text: you will not solicit, divert, or attempt to solicit or divert any actual or potential business or customer of the Franchised Business to any Competitive Business.
rationale: Customer non-solicit protects company; "solicit, divert, or attempt to solicit" is standard and restricts only franchisee.

text: Any period of non-compliance with the requirements of this Section 19, whether such non-compliance takes place after termination, expiration, non-renewal, and/or a transfer, will not be credited toward satisfying the two-year obligation specified above.
rationale: Tolling clause; "will not be credited" favors company and restricts franchisee, not company activity.

text: Section 19.3.3 above will not apply to your ownership of less than five percent (5%) beneficial interest in the outstanding equity securities of any publicly-held corporation.
rationale: Passive carve-out for "less than five percent (5%)" of public companies is market-standard and limited in scope.

text: You agree to require and obtain execution of covenants similar to those set forth in Sections 9.3, 11, 16, 18 above, and this Section 19 (as modified to apply to an individual), from your Managers, Producers and other managerial and/or executive staff, as well as your Principals.
rationale: Requires franchisee to obtain covenants from its staff; "You agree to require and obtain" places obligation on franchisee.

text: You agree that during the term of this Agreement, except as we have otherwise approved in writing, you (or the Operating Principal or Manager) will devote full time, energy, and best efforts to the management and operation of the Franchised Business.
rationale: Full-time, best-efforts obligation on franchisee; "except as we have otherwise approved" is a standard franchisee duty, not company exclusivity.

text: you agree to pay to us, as liquidated damages, an amount calculated as follows:
rationale: Rule: pre-set damages need legal approval. "as liquidated damages, an amount calculated as follows" sets a formula requiring enforceability review.

text: You agree that the existence of any claims you may have against us, whether or not arising from this Agreement, will not constitute a defense to our enforcement of the covenants in this Section 19.
rationale: Rule: waivers of legal remedies need legal approval. "will not constitute a defense" bars franchisee's claims as defenses to enforcement.

text: This Agreement takes effect when we accept and sign this document.
rationale: Flag one-sided obligations: "when we accept and sign" lets the company control when the agreement takes effect.

text: This Agreement will be interpreted and construed exclusively under the laws of the State of Texas, which laws will prevail in the event of any conflict of law (without regard to, and without giving effect to, the application of Texas choice-of-law rules);
rationale: Market-standard choice of law; "exclusively under the laws of the State of Texas" likely matches the company's home jurisdiction.

text: Any transfer by SpinCo or a member of its Group shall require the transferee to agree pursuant to a written agreement to maintain any trade secrets and Information included in the transferred Intellectual Property in strict confidence.

text: Parent and members of the Parent Group shall be made third party beneficiaries under such transfer agreement to enforce breaches of the license.
